pleioverse

Fast, self-contained simulation and testing for pleiotropic genetic data.

pleioverse is an R package for simulating multi-phenotype genetic architectures and running a broad suite of multi-phenotype association and pleiotropy tests. The package is organized around one S4 pleio object, so the typical workflow is simple:

  1. simulate data with run_pleiosim();
  2. test the simulated variants with run_pleiotest(), or run selected methods one at a time;
  3. inspect the accumulated result columns in pleio@results.

The aliases pleiosim() and pleiotest() call the same underlying functions.

Installation

Install from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("broccolito/pleioverse")

You will need R package-building tools, a C++17-capable compiler, and the Rcpp and RcppArmadillo packages. On macOS this usually means installing Xcode Command Line Tools. On Linux, install the standard R development toolchain for your distribution.

Usage 

library(pleioverse)

set.seed(1)

pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 3,
  n_participant = 10000,
  n_variant_pleiotropic = 10,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(10, 10, 10),
  n_variant_null = 960,
  heritability = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
)

pleio <- run_pleiotest(pleio)
head(pleio@results)

Run only the methods you need:

pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 2,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(10, 10),
  heritability = c(0.2, 0.2)
)

pleio <- pleio |>
  run_wald() |>
  run_vc() |>
  run_placo(i = 1, j = 2)

head(pleio@results)

Combine existing p-value columns with run_acat():

pleio <- run_acat(pleio, cols = c("wald", "vc", "placo"))
head(pleio@results$acat)

Main Functions

Task Functions
Simulate a complete pleio object run_pleiosim()
Build simulation input matrices create_heritable_correlation_matrix(), create_nonheritable_correlation_matrix(), create_cohort_makeup_matrix(), create_eaf_matrix(), create_efs_matrix_template()
Run the default suite run_pleiotest()
Run common multiple-association tests run_wald(), run_vc(), run_sum(), run_minp(), run_tates(), run_metacca()
Run pleiotropy-focused tests run_placo(), run_pgctest(), run_maiup(), run_conjfdr(), run_polarmorphism()
Aggregate completed result columns run_acat()

Result Object

run_pleiosim() returns an S4 object of class pleio. It stores the simulation settings, genotype and phenotype products, summary statistics, and the result table populated by run_pleiotest() or by individual method functions.

Important result groups are encoded in the variant names:

  • pleio_variant*: variants associated with all phenotypes;
  • nonpleio_variant*: variants associated with one phenotype;
  • null_variant*: variants with no simulated phenotype effect.

Development

Install the package locally from the repository root:

R CMD INSTALL .

Run the test suite:

Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(".")'

Build the documentation website:

Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'

The package uses C++17, Rcpp, and RcppArmadillo for the computational core. Files in dev/ are local parity, baseline, and timing scripts; they are not part of the installed R package.

Method Sources

The statistical methods implemented or mirrored by pleioverse are grounded in the following linked sources:

  • Liu and Lin (2018), multiple phenotype association tests using summary statistics in GWAS, Biometrics. DOI
  • Liu and Lin (2019), principal-component association tests in multiple phenotype studies, Journal of the American Statistical Association. DOI
  • Luo et al. (2020), MTAR multi-trait rare-variant summary-statistic analysis, Nature Communications. DOI
  • Liu and Xie (2019), Cauchy combination test, Journal of the American Statistical Association. DOI
  • Liu et al. (2019), ACAT rare-variant p-value combination, American Journal of Human Genetics. DOI
  • Wu et al. (2011), SKAT, American Journal of Human Genetics. DOI
  • Lee, Wu, and Lin (2012), optimal rare-variant tests, Biostatistics. DOI
  • van der Sluis, Posthuma, and Dolan (2013), TATES, PLoS Genetics. DOI
  • Li et al. (2011), GATES extended Simes procedure, American Journal of Human Genetics. DOI
  • Cichonska et al. (2016), metaCCA, Bioinformatics. DOI
  • Ray and Chatterjee (2020), PLACO, PLoS Genetics. DOI
  • Andreassen et al. (2013), conditional FDR, PLoS Genetics. DOI
  • Smeland et al. (2020), conditional FDR for shared loci, Human Genetics. DOI
  • von Berg et al. (2022), PolarMorphism, Bioinformatics. DOI
  • Kessy, Lewin, and Strimmer (2018), whitening and decorrelation, The American Statistician. DOI
  • Conneely and Boehnke (2007), correlated-test p-value adjustment, American Journal of Human Genetics. DOI
  • Davies (1980), linear combinations of chi-square random variables, Applied Statistics. DOI
  • Liu, Tang, and Zhang (2009), chi-square approximation for quadratic forms, Computational Statistics & Data Analysis. DOI
  • Zeng et al., MAIUP software reference. Repository
